items.text: Excellent points. Sad to see people down voting you. I'm glad Waterloo and Kitchener have removed Fluorine from the water supply and hope it stays that way! If enough people really want fluorine in their water, maybe water filtration companies will produce a product that allows someone the CHOICE to add fluorine to their water. People who strongly believe that it is harming them should not be forced to ingest it.

Buddy, if you want fluoride in your water so badly, then add it yourself. Why are you trying to force people who strongly believe it affects their health to take it? You have to be very arrogant to assume that your side is indisputably correct, and to coerce everyone to do what you think is best. There is plenty of science on both sides, so the fair thing to do here is give people the choice of what they ingest. Even if you are correct, does that make it right to force this on people who disagree, even if they're not right? The courteous thing to do is to offer your opinion, and give people the freedom to decide for themselves, not force them to ingest what you think is safe. Maybe you and a group of others who agree with you can convince a private filter company to offer a product variant that allows you to dilute fluoride into your own water?

Yes, exactly! Give people the CHOICE of what they ingest!! It's extremely arrogant for people to force others to ingest what they think is safe, with complete disregard to what the other person thinks...it's just a basic matter of freedom and personal choice that is being infringed upon.
Ok Mao.
Let's hope that with the Ford PCs and the Scheer feds we kill SJW culture.

items.title: $100 ish neutral speakers for classical / youtube videos?
items.text:
$100 ish neutral speakers for classical / youtube videos?
Hi, can I please get suggestions for a basic speaker setup, on my desk, for my computer? I just want to listen to classical music or watch YouTube videos without the bass being overpowering, as seems to be the case on many speakers today, which is unfortunate...I want a neutral playback, so I can hear what the music is supposed to sound like.

It doesn't have to be loud at all. This honestly seems like it shouldn't be such a hard thing to find, but I just bought $109 bose from [amazon.ca](https://amazon.ca) and the bass is ridiculous...I'm from Canada BTW

&#x200B;

Budget is around $100-$150 ish. Wired solutions only, please. I am not interested in wireless/bluetooth compatibility.  


These are the Bose I am disappointed with:  


[https://www.amazon.ca/Companion-Multimedia-Speakers-3-5mm-input/dp/B00CD1PTF0/ref=sr\_1\_fkmrnull\_2?keywords=edifier+exclaim+e10&qid=1554403098&s=gateway&sr=8-2-fkmrnull](https://www.amazon.ca/Companion-Multimedia-Speakers-3-5mm-input/dp/B00CD1PTF0/ref=sr_1_fkmrnull_2?keywords=edifier+exclaim+e10&qid=1554403098&s=gateway&sr=8-2-fkmrnull)

&#x200B;

I can't say I know the difference. I just want basic computer speakers, except I don't want to hear overpowered bass.  


These are the Bose  


[https://www.amazon.ca/Companion-Multimedia-Speakers-3-5mm-input/dp/B00CD1PTF0/ref=sr\_1\_2?keywords=bose+companion&qid=1554402763&s=gateway&sr=8-2](https://www.amazon.ca/Companion-Multimedia-Speakers-3-5mm-input/dp/B00CD1PTF0/ref=sr_1_2?keywords=bose+companion&qid=1554402763&s=gateway&sr=8-2)
Thanks. Looking over the FAQ, it looks like I'm looking for active speakers, as I need them to plug into my blue yeti microphone (the sound card on my motherboard broke, lol)

You're right, R1000T4 is not available in Canada. I don't need Bluetooth...I might be able to get away with the bigger ones, but just in case I need compact, do you think this version is any good?  


[https://www.amazon.ca/Edifier-R980T-Active-Bookshelf-Speakers/dp/B01LXDZ8WB/ref=cm\_cr\_arp\_d\_product\_top?ie=UTF8](https://www.amazon.ca/Edifier-R980T-Active-Bookshelf-Speakers/dp/B01LXDZ8WB/ref=cm_cr_arp_d_product_top?ie=UTF8)

What about even Logitech? Are they just trash? I like their mice and keyboards...  


Something like this?  


[https://www.amazon.ca/Logitech-Channel-Computer-Speaker-980-000800/dp/B00EZ9XKCM/ref=sr\_1\_1?keywords=logitech+speakers&qid=1554415971&s=gateway&sr=8-1](https://www.amazon.ca/Logitech-Channel-Computer-Speaker-980-000800/dp/B00EZ9XKCM/ref=sr_1_1?keywords=logitech+speakers&qid=1554415971&s=gateway&sr=8-1)

I got the r980t from Amazon...wow they're amazing!! SO much better than Bose! Everything instantly sounds lighter and a lot more clear and articulate...thank you so much for recommending Edifier. I'm glad I got the compact version, because I have an ultrawide 34" monitor, so it takes up a lot of desk space. The r980t is already bigger than the bose...anything bigger than this would certainly not be ideal. Thanks again! So happy I finally found some speakers that just play music without so much BASS!!

They're still not perfect, but leagues ahead of the Bose. Maybe one day when I can get a shelf installed I'll upgrade them to the bigger set. I think I see what you mean about the bass coming out front...it still feels a bit too present for my liking...overall very happy, though, and there's a nob on the back to turn the bass down.
Glad to see the people getting involved in this issue.

It's definitely better, but I of course like to hear a normal amount of bass, as it's a part of the music, so I don't have it down too much. I think I'd just prefer having it fire in the rear so that it feels like more of the background rather than foreground. I can definitely live with what I've got now, though, as it's great all around.

You're going to think I'm crazy, but I'd rather avoid the bluetooth. I'm trying to limit EMF exposure in my house. Also, I think those ones are bigger, aren't they? Might be tough to fit on my desk with my ultrawide monitor. That is a very good deal, though, thanks for showing me.

Oh, I see. I just figured there would be some ambient EMF radiation from the bluetooth, even with it off, and I didn't realize that you could choose to connect that model through wire. Well, if there's no EMF concern, then I agree and will probably replace mine this weekend...save some money and get a better pair of speakers?? Why not : ). I appreciate all your help, you've been very helpful.

Hey, I'm considering purchasing these today. Just wondering if you're sure they're any better sounding. What is it about them that makes them sound better? Also, where do you see that it has a rear firing port?  


Still a bit worried about any possible EMF from the bluetooth, even when it's turned off...never know if it's completely off, if you know what I mean.

I know this comment was made in jest, but I'd like to share a video I found about this, which I found was very informative. Basically, the guy is saying that a sure fire way to fight global warming is to reverse desertification through mimicking nature. We can use livestock to herd and graze over lands of poor condition in order to restore them and trap water and CO2 in the Earth.  


[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vpTHi7O66pI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vpTHi7O66pI)
Are you sure about the rear firing port, though? I don't see that in the description anywhere?

Oh, I see! So that's what that is. Actually, I think the Bose had that, as well.  


I just read that rear bass ports don't do as well as front facing ones when the speakers are near a wall, which mine unfortunately are (although I know that it's not ideal, it's just how my current setup is). So, I think I'll just stick with the R980T until my situation changes, in which case I'll probably invest in a better surround sound system, anyway.  


Thanks for all your help, friend. Have a wonderful day.

I found an interesting forum thread, detailing how the placement of the port actually has no impact on the sound, as long as it's designed correctly. So maybe what you're experiencing is simply a speaker that has an overall design that you prefer over your previous front ported speakers, but the placement of the port itself is apparently inconsequential :).

https://www.talkbass.com/threads/cabinets-front-ported-vs-sealed-vs-rear-ported.532968/
I'm a web developer...so I'm someone who actually might use this service, if only they didn't pester me so much with their ads!! Forget about it now, there's no way I'll ever give them any money.

items.title: When to buy a house?
items.text:
When to buy a house?
I'm considering buying a house around the Waterloo region soon. However, I have two concerns.

1. When the real estate bubble pops, which I'm thinking will either be this year or next year, I'll get hosed
2. Even if the bubble does pop next year, it'll take about 5 years for prices to return to the trend line, during which I'll be blowing money on rent.

Thoughts? We are first time home buyers.

If you look at this chart, it certainly looks like this region has suffered from inflated housing prices, just like the rest of Canada has. All bubbles deflate in their entirety, and eventually return to the trend line. In fact, prices may even go below the trend line for a period, if bankers are pessimistic enough about lending.  


[https://imgur.com/a/r2V3kuI](https://imgur.com/a/r2V3kuI)  


Yes, but it would still be a loss. Sure, the price of the house would come back to today's price, but that will be due to inflation. The real value will not increase.

It happened to several countries in 2007/2008, including the U.S, Ireland, Portugal and Spain. Fortunately, our banks weren't quite as aggressive as theirs, but we certainly did bail them out. Since then, the price of our houses in real terms have continued to rise, and are currently about 30% more expensive than houses were in the States at the peak of their bubble. I just can't see us sustaining this for very much longer.

I think you might be under the illusion of wealth, due to inflation. Certainly, if you sell now, at the apex of the bubble, you will come out ahead. However, once the bubble fully deflates, the real value of your house will not have increased. The price will be higher, but if you correct for inflation, the real value is about the same.

Well, if the housing market crashes, that will likely have a serious impact on the economy, since Canada has invested so much in housing. I'm not planning on losing my job, but anything can happen during a recession. It would suck to have a big mortgage to pay off after getting fired.
Still...it's money gained if I just wait for the bubble to pop and get a discounted home, no? I could use that gained money for investments in stocks and bonds.
Holy crap!!!
